title: Handoff Coda: SLO Regression Root Cause + Playbook Updates
content:
Summary:
This is the post-handoff summary and working playbook update after last weekend's latency regression that impacted hosted/api route: text.generate.v1. The goal of this doc is to leave a clear, actionable handoff for the next on-call rotation, capture a short RCA, and propose small playbook changes we can land quickly (and note longer-term follow ups).

High-level impact:
- Time window: 2026-09-19 03:40 UTC -> 2026-09-19 05:10 UTC (services showed elevated p95 latency).
- Affected surface: hosted API (text.generate.v1), small spike in 5xx errors for multi-region customers served via smart-routing fallback.
- Customer visible effect: ~7% of requests saw >2s extra latency; error rate increased from 0.3% to 1.4% at peak.
- SLO bump: p95 latency SLO (<= 350ms) breached for two 10-minute windows; error SLO still within burn budget but trending.

Immediate timeline (condensed):
- 03:38 UTC: first latency alerts from synthetic p95 probes in us-central1 (alert threshold: p95 > 350ms for 3m).
- 03:42 UTC: on-call (Aisha) paged, began triage in #sre-ops.
- 03:45 UTC: cross-region traces show increased kernel scheduling on GPU hosts; queue length on inference worker nodes increased.
- 03:55 UTC: mitigation #1 — temporarily tighten batching window on dedicated pools serving hosted traffic (reduced batch delay from 12ms->6ms) to lower tail latency; partial improvement observed.
- 04:15 UTC: Identified upstream change: autoscaler API returned stale available-capacity for a subset of dedicated pools due to recent cache invalidation change in autoscaler service (PR merged REDWOOD-3421).
- 04:30 UTC: mitigation #2 — manual restart of autoscaler agents in affected region to flush stale state; routing controller rebalanced traffic.
- 05:10 UTC: latency returned to baseline.

Root cause (short):
- Trigger: regression introduced in autoscaler caching layer (REDWOOD-3421) that caused ~12% of autoscaler agents to report outdated free-slot counts under certain TTL renewal races.
- Effect: traffic routing decisions directed excess load to fewer inference pools, increasing load per host and causing queueing at the runtime layer (longer KV cache warmups and larger batch sizes forming).
- Contributing factors: insufficient end-to-end test coverage for distributed cache race conditions; lack of a pre-deploy chaos test that simulates TTL/skew on autoscaler cache.

Postmortem notes / evidence to attach:
- Traces: trace ids collected in linked_artifacts (see JIRA REDWOOD-3421 for raw traces).
- Host metrics: cpu/gpu queue depth charts for affected pools (saved to REDWOOD-3421 artifacts).
- Autoscaler agent logs: show TTL renewal failing ~03:32 UTC with repeated 503s to cache service.

Temporary changes landed during incident:
- Manual redeploy of autoscaler agents for two affected regions.
- Adjusted batching window for implicated dedicated pools (reverted after incident).
- Added short-lived synthetic canary targeting newly merged autoscaler change in a canary region.

Playbook action items (short-term, ranked):
1) Hotfix the autoscaler caching retry logic (owner: Carlos Gomez, JIRA REDWOOD-3478). Targeting a small patch to add exponential backoff and stronger TTL reconciliation. ETA: 2026-09-24.
2) Add alerting for autoscaler agent divergence: new metric "autoscaler_agent_stale_percent" > 5% over 2m should page SRE (owner: Liam O'Connor). ETA: 2026-09-23.
3) Update on-call runbook: add step to check autoscaler agent state and per-pool free-slot consistency when p95 latency rises (owner: Aisha Patel). ETA: 2026-09-22 (landed as draft).
4) Create unit+integration test that simulates cache TTL skew and validates reconcilers reconcile to correct counts (owner: runtime QA). ETA: 2026-10-05.
5) Run a small chaos experiment for cache-service availability to validate autoscaler resiliency (owner: eng-chaos). ETA: 2026-10-12.

Playbook updates (text to insert into runbook):
- On latency alert for text.generate.v1: first check routing controller diagnostics -> per-pool free-slot distribution -> autoscaler agent logs -> cache-service latency. If free-slot skew observed, proceed to agent restart play; if not, proceed to runtime-level diagnosis.
- Quick mitigation checklist (ordered):
  1) Reduce batch delay on high-latency pools (temporary).
  2) Check autoscaler agent status (ps, last-sync timestamp).
  3) Restart autoscaler agents in region (rolling, 1 agent at a time).
  4) If autoscaler restart not helpful, temporarily divert traffic to alternate region or model variant.

SLO status and risk assessment:
- p95 latency (text.generate.v1): breached briefly, incurred ~0.02% SLO burn for the week.
- Error SLO: within budget but monitor next 7 days for regressions tied to autoscaler changes.
- Risk: moderate until autoscaler cache fix lands; potential for recurrence if cache service experiences increased latency.

Notes to next on-call:
- Priority: ensure REDWOOD-3478 patch merges and a canary is running. Watch for autoscaler_agent_stale_percent alarms.
- If you see a p95 spike and autoscaler agents look healthy, skip immediate restarts and escalate to runtime team (Emily Chen) — we've seen cases where runtime-level KV cache warmups dominate tail latency.
- Slack tip: use /quickrun reroute-hosted to move small traffic slices to dedicated backup region while debugging.

Follow-ups (longer-term):
- Add a post-merge pipeline job that runs a cache-ttl-skew scenario against autoscaler in staging.
- Improve synthetic probes to include a regional per-pool free-slot checker rather than only end-to-end p95.
- Consider moving autoscaler state reconciliation to a quorum-based approach instead of single-agent authoritative counts.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How often does autoscaler cache service see transient 5xxs? Need longer-term metrics (assigned to Observability).
- Can we safely lower default batching window for all hosted pools without cost regressions? Product needs to weigh tail-latency vs token cost.
- Do we want an automated fallback routing rule if N% of agents report stale state for >X minutes? (proposal from routing team).

Action owners & short checklist (for immediate sprint):
- Carlos: implement REDWOOD-3478 hotfix, create PR, request expedited review.
- Liam: define and land autoscaler_agent_stale_percent metric + alert.
- Aisha: update runbook and add triage checklist, run a quick 1:1 with on-call for next handoff.
- Emily: review runtime warmup tradeoffs and advise on safe lower bound for batch delay.

Appendix: raw handoff note posted to #sre-ops at 05:30 UTC:
"latency incident resolved; root cause autoscaler cache TTL race from recent merge REDWOOD-3421. Hotfix REDWOOD-3478 in progress. Watch autoscaler_agent_stale_percent; if >5% in any region page eng-sre on-call. Restarting agents in region X fixed routing imbalance. Follow-up items listed in REDWOOD-3478."

Quick retrospective (lessons learned):
- Small changes in control-plane caching can have outsize effects on serving economics; need tighter canarying of control-plane changes.
- Runbooks benefited troubleshooting speed but lacked the autoscaler-specific checks; minimal runbook update would have shaved ~12 minutes off time-to-mitigation.
- Cross-team visibility (routing/runtime/autoscaler) was solid; slack channels and traces made coordination fast.

If anything else needed in the handoff, ping me (Aisha) or see the linked JIRA for artifacts.

"Notes to self": keep this doc short and pragmatic; avoid full RCA format here — a full postmortem will be filed once REDWOOD-3478 is confirmed and merged.
